questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. That my destination was student-friendly in terms of ambience/environment and price/cost. 
2. The possibility to study and experience a different country's law system in general.
3. That the city is beautiful and nice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy. I rarely felt like I was missing certain information, and when I did, I got that information from other exchange-students who had the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Did not receive any assistance from Erasmus or host university when arriving.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The introduction to the host university was very sparesome. We had a brief walk-around the faculty and a presentation with information, but then that was it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was very easy as I didn't want to restrict myself economically. As so, it was easy to find something to my liking. I found my accommodation through AirBnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there are various WhatsApp-groups where people can help each other to find accommodations. This would be nice to know beforehand, but it would be difficult to share these WhatsApp-groups, as they are established by students who comes and goes in relation to exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of information to take note of, but since I managed to get through it all I guess it was ok.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an acceptance-registration which was quite thorough. Once accepted and at the university, the enrolling in courses was fairly easy to manage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Unsure what to answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I'd say 80% succesful. I didn't get all the classes I had envisaged beforehand, but I got the ones most important for me, and the new ones were nice as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Students should know, that the enrollment/registration is a 'first come, first served' system, which can come as a surprise for many people. I didn't know beforehand, that you absolutely had to be ready at the specific time when registration opened to make sure you got the classes you wanted. This is crucial information for many students, as some relies on having specific classes during their exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a wide range of different courses which was good. I did not like the way the courses were weighted in ECTS. It felt silly to have a lot of different classes which only amounted to 3 and 6 ECTS each. You learned a lot of different stuff very superficially.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied a lot from class to class. Some classes were very thorough while others were at a very low academic level. By this I mean, that some of the classes didn't require or involved any actual juridical method, it was just a matter of remembering information. Therefore keeping the level at a explanatory and not analytical level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly lecture-based, with the teacher arriving and speaking singlehandedly for the duration of the class. At UCPH, we mostly have seminars where the focus is more on working actively with cases where our skills can be trained and enhanced. This was not the same at CU. I believe the way of teaching at UCPH is way more beneficial for the students, and would prefer this way of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law
- Theories of Legal Personhood
- Financial Law
- Private Law
- Natural Resource Law
- Intellectual Property Law
- Czech Legal History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The course "Legal Reasoning: First Amendment Case Law". 
I would recommend this course, as it's really interesting and the teacher is phenomenal. He incites exciting and critical debates amongst the students. It was a really giving course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No answer.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries. These were as some of the only things not more cheap than back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't attend any but appreciate the opportunities provided.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Some events were arranged at my faculty which were very cool (like a night party, and a debate).
I also attended a traditional Scandinavian Christmas arrangement at another faculty which was nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are MANY activities you can attend, so just attend what you would like to be honest.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit neighbouring countries by bus.

Try Escape-Rooms! Prague is very good at making them!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialize a lot with local students. Mostly other exchange-students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None were particularly difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy-going, laid back vibe. No one seemed to be stressed. I liked that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for the costs of Denmark in general (quite expensive for people not from Scandinavia).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get in the various WhatsApp groups that exists, as you can meet many new people there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having fun and experiencing the city+country with other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Social fatigue. At some point you get burned out. But you should not worry as it's totally natural and it's OK to take a breather and not attend every event that occurs.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
